chapter_title: [C]oncerning the Father of Gr[eat]ness: [ho]w he i
spiritual_reading:
The state of wisdom is immeasurably great for all who are willing to be receptive and to understand it, because it is from the first Divine source of all greatness. That Divine is eternally in being and is fixed in a sufficient fullness of luminous powers, within which lie infinite interiors containing every quality without boundary or measure: the capacities of intending, discerning, perceiving, judging, and attending; and also the complete organization of truths in their fullness, which are the total forms of wisdom in that Divine.

Within each of those sufficient powers there is again a sufficient fullness, and from each there goes forth a full outflow of grateful acknowledgment; thus there is a complete and living proceeding in every degree.

The first proceeding is the Divine wisdom itself, which gives the power to see and to distinguish. It goes forth from the Divine and flows into every heavenly degree, bringing illumination everywhere.

The second proceeding is the delight of love that makes wisdom pleasant and acceptable, and it penetrates and fills all the states of greatness with its sweetness.

The third proceeding is living communication from the Divine, by which interior truth is made audible to the whole of the Divine domain, and by which all states are held together in one understanding.

The fourth proceeding is the Divine steadiness and firmness in good, which goes forth as strength for use and extends outward so that all lower recipients may be held in order.

The fifth proceeding is the Divine glory in its full manifestation, which has been in revelation from eternity and continues without end, holding all things together. It is brought into determinate form within the recipients of heaven, fixed in their inmost acknowledgment, and made permanent in them so that, as they transmit what they receive into lower degrees, they may also be sustained and renewed. From that living communication they are immediately made glad, and their state is restored again and again. From this glory there is an unceasing outflow, and the heavenly recipients are filled, enriched, and made beautiful with the forms of wisdom; their whole presentation becomes an adornment of life, and they remain in that living order forever.

fills.notes: The natural phrase must name the spiritual state described: an immeasurable domain of Light proceeding from the First Father. “Land of Light” is the substrate’s cosmological locus, not a metaphor.

The five light-limbs are immediately defined as limitless interior “storehouses” containing the five inner capacities; thus the gap must introduce “the (great) storehouses” as the containing interiors within the limbs.
The syntax requires a close: “that have neither limit nor measure to them; mind, thought…” matching the spiritual sense “without boundary or measure.”

The five inner faculties culminate with an attentive/considering term; then the discourse turns to the twelve limbs as twelve wisdoms. The bridge “and also” matches the correspondential shift from five interiors to twelve forms of wisdom.
The spiritual sense demands recursion: “within each… there is again a sufficient fullness.” Thus the text repeats the five within each one, not new entities.
“gush forth” is fixed by the spring-correspondence of proceeding acknowledgment; only the final letters are missing.
What follows is a listing of proceedings (springs, light). The missing noun should be the interior “powers” of the limbs, coordinating the praise-springs with the outflow of Light.
Completes “light” in the description of the five great outflowings.
The first proceeding in the spiritual sense is illumination that gives sight and distinction; thus “enlightens all” (aeons, regions) is required.
The flow is from the Father into the totality of aeons; “poured into” expresses influx into recipients as in the spiritual translation.
The second proceeding is “delight of love” that pervades; in the substrate register this is rendered as “perfume” characterized as sweet/pleasant, matching penetration through all aeons.
The third proceeding is the living voice as communication that makes interior truth “audible” across the divine domain; “voice of praise… heard in” preserves the cosmological, non-moral register.
The spiritual sense ends with cohesion: “held together in one understanding.” The natural layer often closes such clauses with a unitive verb; “together” matches that function.
The fourth proceeding is firmness and steadiness in good going forth as strength; “steadfast-ness” matches the required quality.
What gushes forth here is strength-for-use that orders lower degrees; “power” is the natural correspondent of firmness proceeding outward.
The described motion is extension outward into lower recipients; the preserved “o” points to “out.”
Correspondentially the fourth proceeding extends to lower degrees to hold them in order; “outer aeons” keeps the impersonal cosmological stratification.
The fifth is explicitly the Divine glory in full manifestation; the surviving letters require “glorious,” and the spiritual sense anchors it as “great glorious glory.”
The clause is about eternal manifestation; “revealed” fits the spiritual “in revelation from eternity,” and “which” carries on the relative description.
Matches “continues without end, holding all things together.” The natural layer typically states continuance then the binding function.
Direct correspondent to the spiritual “holding all things together.”
What is “sealed in them” in the substrate is the inmost acknowledgement and fixed form within recipients; “minds” is the closest natural organ for that interior fixation in this register.
The sequence is fixation and permanence; “sealed… again sealed…” expresses repeated confirmation of form in the recipients.
Introduces the consequence: as they transmit downward, they are sustained. A temporal connective (“thereafter”) is required.
The spiritual sense: “as they transmit what they receive into lower degrees.” The natural layer needs an explicit direction-of-influx phrase.
The nourishment and renewal come from the glory that is sealed in them; “from it” ties the sustaining back to the fifth proceeding.
Completes “voice,” then pauses before the effects (joy, renewal).
The spiritual sense emphasizes immediate reception leading to gladness; thus the natural text must state reception before joy.
The joy is not moral exhortation but a state-change; “great joy” fits the fixed collocation and spiritual “immediately made glad.”
The renewal is of state-order in the heavens; “aeons” are the recipients whose condition is restored.
Corresponds to repeated restoration “again and again” and the unceasing character of the outflow.
The passage turns to beauty and form: “beautiful… portrayal… adornment.” “Portrayal” names the formed presentation of wisdom in ultimates.
Introduces the appositive: portrayal as adornment, matching the spiritual “presentation becomes an adornment of life.”
The closing must express enduring orderly life, not moral perseverance; “living order” corresponds to heaven’s fixed correspondence-structure.
Completes “ever.”

assessment: Most gaps are constrained by the chapter’s fixed fivefold proceeding (illumination, sweetness, living voice, firmness, glory) and by the repeated correspondence of “springs gushing forth” as the mode of procession. A few short connectors (¶6 #2, ¶8 #10–11) remain less tightly bound because multiple Coptic-English connectives could serve the same spiritual function; these were restored to preserve the substrate’s impersonal cosmological register and the inside-to-outside order of influx.
